title: Modules, Namespaces and Packages
oneLiner: Organising code across files: C# namespaces, using and assemblies, Python modules, packages and imports, the entry point and if __name__ == "__main__", and installing packages with NuGet and pip in a virtual environment.
keyTakeaway: C# namespaces are names only; every file in a project compiles together and using shortens names. A Python module is a file and a package is a folder; import runs a module once and caches it. Guard script code with if __name__ == "__main__", and give each Python project its own virtual environment.
explanation:
Real programs don't fit in one file. This lesson covers how each language splits code into named pieces and brings them back together, and how to use other people's code.

In C#, types are grouped into namespaces such as System.Text, which become part of each type's full name, and a using line lets you leave the namespace off. Namespaces don't care which file or folder code is in: all the files of a project compile together into one assembly, a .dll or .exe, and projects reference each other's assemblies.

In Python the file is the unit: a module is a .py file, a package is a folder of them, and import finds a module by name, runs it once and caches it. Because importing runs the file, scripts guard their start-up code with if __name__ == "__main__": so the same file can also be imported by other code and by tests.

Finally, packages from the internet: NuGet for .NET and pip with PyPI for Python, and why every Python project should have its own virtual environment so different projects' packages don't clash.
